stem: Gordon Allport's trait theory of personality classifies traits into three types based on how dominant and pervasive they are in an individual: a single trait that dominates almost all behaviour (rare), a smaller number of traits that broadly characterise the person, and specific, situation-dependent traits. These three types are respectively called:
explanation: Allport distinguished Cardinal traits (dominate whole personality), Central traits (core describing traits), and Secondary traits (situation-specific).
